inputs.share_count_basis: 266,109,685 shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (H1-2026 balance sheet; 268,564,630 issued less 2,454,945 treasury). Basic = diluted EPS in H1-2026 (LTIP is largely cash-settled), so outstanding is the fully diluted count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the remaining ~EUR503m of the 2026 EUR1bn buyback (to May 2027) and the EUR523m buyback-mandate liability are both left out (value-neutral at a near-fair price; ~12-13m further shares would retire).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 equity-settled share-based payment EUR8.2m (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp, from the 20-F). EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year. The cash-settled LTIP/Performance Share plans run through personnel expense and are already inside EBITDA.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury stock EUR585.3m (cash-flow statement); a further EUR347m in Q1 2026, and a second EUR1bn program running to May 2027. The flat share count is being funded: FME is an active repurchaser.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the reporting currency of the flows: 10y Bund ~2.7% + equity beta ~1.0 x 5.5% ERP = CoE ~8.2%; pre-tax cost of financial debt ~3.8% (EUR/USD bonds) x (1-26%) = ~2.8%; weights ~62/38 equity/financial debt at market (leases are in the flows, so excluded from the debt weight) give ~6.2%. Rounded UP to 7.0% because ~70% of the flows are USD earned and translated (USD rates higher than EUR), not as a stacked risk premium. Same WACC in every scenario: regulatory/reimbursement risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease cash (FY2025 principal EUR649.0m [623.3 unrelated + 25.7 related] + interest on lease liabilities EUR143.2m = EUR792m, 4.0% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path inside EBIT. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total 1,500.4 less ROU depreciation 647.6 and ROU impairment 15.4 = ~837, 4.3%). Lease liabilities (EUR3,397.4m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. The company's own net debt (EUR9,902m) includes them; ours (EUR6,504.6m) does not, by design.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of the US clinic JVs); NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 11x LTM NCI net income (FY2025 212.9 - H1-25 85.4 + H1-26 122.0 = EUR249.5m, ~2,745). Book NCI is only EUR974.5m because the puttable NCI sits in liabilities under IFRS; the earnings multiple covers both, so the put-option liability is NOT deducted separately. NCI distributions run EUR314m/yr in a normal year (EUR574m in FY2025 incl. the Interwell put settlement).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (leases, NCI, pension). Routing: FME is an operating healthcare-services and medical-device company (dialysis clinics plus product manufacturing), not a bank/REIT/holdco, so the owner-FCF row applies; no MEMORY.md entry, this is the first valuation. EBITDA here is the reported IFRS-16 figure (FY2025 3,327, 17.0% of revenue), NOT the company's adjusted EBITDA (LTM 3,791), because the EUR450-540m/yr of 'special items' (FME25+ restructuring, portfolio exits) has recurred every year since 2021. last_fcf follows the contract formula (reported FCF = OCF 2,681.0 - capex 915.4; less SBC 8.2; no interest-income strip because FME carries net debt), but note it is BEFORE lease principal (649) and NCI distributions (~314), both of which this model charges elsewhere (lease line in the flows, NCI in the bridge). It is a levered, pre-lease, pre-NCI figure and overstates the owner's cash. FY2025 cash tax paid (EUR226m) was abnormally low against 445/410 in FY2024/FY2023; the model uses a normal 26% unlevered cash rate (US federal+state ~25%, Germany ~30%). The EUR/USD translation effect is in the revenue path: FY2026 guidance is flat revenue at constant currency, but at the guided 1.18 EUR/USD reported EUR revenue falls ~2-3% (H1-26 9,473 vs H1-25 9,673, -2.1%). Near SBC-zero filer: house and street bases are almost identical (SBC 0.04% of revenue).
inputs.sbc_projection_note: SBC-zero treatment: equity-settled SBC is EUR8.2m (0.04% of revenue) and the cash-settled LTIP already runs through EBITDA, so the forward SBC row is held explicit at 0%. House and street bases therefore coincide, and band_position is null (the band collapses). Charging the 0.04% would cost ~EUR0.6/share (<1%) and would only produce a degenerate band reading (about -3,500% on the first build).

equity_bridge.item: Noncontrolling interests at 11x LTM NCI net income (EUR249.5m)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 20-F income statement line 12270 (212.9) and H1-2026 interim line 1841 (122.0 vs 85.4); book NCI 974.5 at 30 Jun 2026 understates because puttable NCI is classified as a liability

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.5% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR -3.2% and revenue 5yr 1.9%. Equity growth is held down by the EUR1bn buyback and FX translation (OCI -1,356m in FY2025); EPS 5yr is distorted by the 2020 COVID/CARES-Act peak; the 3yr EPS CAGR of 13.5% is margin recovery off the 2022 trough (7.9% OI margin), not volume growth. The forward base path (~3.4% revenue CAGR after a translation-hit FY2026) leans on the CMD 3-7% aspiration's low end, not on any trailing figure.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF less SBC) CAGRs are almost identical to reported (6.8% vs 6.9% 3yr) because SBC is only ~EUR8m: SBC is not funding the growth. The 5yr FCF CAGR of -11.2% starts from FY2020's EUR3.18bn, inflated by ~EUR1.6bn of CARES Act Medicare advance payments later repaid; it is not a trend.

base.growth_note: FY2026 = guided flat cc revenue translated at EUR/USD 1.18 (H1 -2.1% reported). FY2027-30 3.5-4.0% = low end of the 2025-28 CMD 3-7% cc aspiration (5008X/HVHDF product pull-through and VBC growth against ~flat US same-market treatments); fades to 2.5%. Trailing reported revenue CAGR is only 0.4% 3yr / 1.9% 5yr (divestitures and FX), so the base deliberately does not take the aspiration's midpoint.
base.margin_note: FY2026 17.4% = H1-26 1,578 + H2-25-like ~1,750 on ~19.1bn (OI guide flat to MSD-negative). Rises ~2pp to 19.5% by FY2033 as FME25+ (EUR1.2bn by 2027) lands and special-item drag fades: about half the way to the mid-teens 2030 OI aspiration, and the midpoint of the post-IFRS-16 range (16.0% FY2023 to 22.9% FY2020).
base.capex_note: Guided EUR0.8-1.0bn/yr 2025-2030; elevated in 2026-27 for the 5008X installed-base swap (H1-26 capex 430), settling at ~D&A ex-ROU.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables-heavy payor model (Medicare/commercial DSO ~70 days) plus product inventory; growth consumes cash.

scenario_narratives.base: 2026 is the guided transition year: flat constant-currency revenue, translated down ~3% into EUR, and operating income roughly flat as EUR250m of FME25+ savings offsets inflation, TDAPA phase-out and ACA-subsidy payor-mix drag. From 2027 the 5008X/HVHDF rollout and Value-Based Care growth take revenue to the low end of the CMD's 3-7% aspiration, while US same-market treatments stay close to flat on GLP-1/SGLT2 and referral softness. The margin recovers about half the way toward the mid-teens 2030 aspiration (reported EBITDA 17.4% to 19.5%) as restructuring special items fade after 2027. The new CEO keeps Reignite broadly intact; the cyberattack has no material operating cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: HVHDF becomes the US standard of care on the CONVINCE mortality data, lifting both product pull-through (Care Enablement to a mid-teens margin) and clinic economics. Interwell Health scales profitably and US payor mix holds despite the ACA subsidy expiry. Revenue runs at the middle of the 3-7% aspiration, and the group reaches roughly the mid-teens operating margin (reported EBITDA ~21.5%, about the FY2020-21 IFRS-16 level). External CEO Korangy speeds up portfolio pruning and capital returns.
scenario_narratives.bear: US reimbursement does the damage: ACA exchange subsidy expiry and the Marietta ruling push commercial patients onto Medicare/Medicaid, OBBBA Medicaid cuts bite, and same-market treatment growth stays negative as GLP-1s slow ESRD incidence. The 5008X conversion runs late and over budget under a new, external CEO, and China volume-based procurement keeps Care Enablement at the bottom of its band. The 2025 margin breakout reverses toward the FY2023 trough (reported EBITDA ~16.2%), revenue grows ~2% nominal, and the exit multiple compresses to 12x for a regulated, ex-growth utility.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the thesis depends on a single regulator (CMS/Medicare plus US policy on ACA and Medicaid), 2026 is an explicit transition year with US treatment guidance already cut mid-year, and the CEO left abruptly in the middle of the largest product launch in the company's history. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right: HVHDF adoption, benign payor mix, and execution under new leadership. Base 50% reflects a non-discretionary, annuity-like demand base and a margin program that has already delivered (EUR804m of savings against a EUR750m target).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A dialysis duopolist priced like a utility whose regulator is also its largest customer. Value depends almost entirely on the margin path, not on volume: the base case gives credit for half of the Reignite margin aspiration and charges the real costs the company's adjusted figures leave out (IFRS-16 lease cash, recurring special items, minority partners' share of the US clinics).
key_risks_to_valuation: US reimbursement policy (CMS ESRD PPS rate, ACA subsidy expiry, OBBBA Medicaid cuts, Marietta) moves the margin path more than any operating lever
NCI valuation: 11x LTM NCI earnings is a judgment; each 1x is ~EUR0.94/share
EUR/USD: ~70% of flows are USD; a 10% stronger euro cuts EUR value roughly pro rata
Leadership transition and 5008X rollout execution in 2026-27
Terminal value is cap-bound at 15x owner FCF in the base case, so most of the value sits beyond 2035
